title: Automate a follow-up with Flow
goal: You will activate an Account-triggered Flow that qualifies new customers, branches on annual revenue, creates a follow-up task, and logs creation failures.
prerequisites: Flow Builder access and permission to activate flows
A custom Flow_Error__c object with Message__c and Record_Id__c text fields
A sandbox or development org with test Account records

steps.action: Create a record-triggered Flow for Account records.
steps.where: Setup > Process Automation > Flows > New Flow > Record-Triggered Flow.
steps.why: The flow needs an Account record-change event as its starting point.
steps.checkpoint: Flow Builder opens with a Start card whose Object is Account.
hint_levels: Start from the Flows list in Setup.
Choose the trigger type that responds to saved records, then select Account.
Click New Flow > Record-Triggered Flow > Create, set Object to Account.

steps.action: Configure the Flow to run after an Account is created or updated when Type equals Customer - Direct and Billing Country is not blank.
steps.where: Start configuration panel under Configure Trigger, Set Entry Conditions, and Optimize the Flow For.
steps.why: Entry conditions prevent irrelevant or incomplete Accounts from entering the automation.
steps.checkpoint: The Start card shows Account, created or updated, two AND conditions, and Actions and Related Records.
hint_levels: Use the Start panel to narrow which saves launch the Flow.
Set Type to Customer - Direct, require BillingCountry to be non-null, and choose the after-save optimization.

In Start, choose A record is created or updated; set Condition Requirements to All Conditions Are Met (AND); add Type Equals Customer - Direct and BillingCountry Is Null False; choose Actions and Related Records; click Done.

steps.action: Set the Flow to run only when an updated Account first meets the entry conditions.
steps.where: Start configuration panel under When to Run the Flow for Updated Records.
steps.why: This prevents repeated task creation on every later edit to an already-qualified Account.
steps.checkpoint: The Start panel shows Only when a record is updated to meet the condition requirements.
hint_levels: Look for the update-run behavior beneath the conditions.
Choose the option that detects the transition from not qualified to qualified.
In Start > When to Run the Flow for Updated Records, select Only when a record is updated to meet the condition requirements, then click Done.

steps.action: Add a Decision named Segment by Revenue with an Enterprise outcome for Annual Revenue greater than or equal to 1000000.
steps.where: Flow canvas Add Element button after Start > Logic > Decision.
steps.why: The decision isolates the high-value branch while leaving missing or smaller revenue values on the default path.
steps.checkpoint: The Decision card shows Enterprise and Default Outcome connectors.
hint_levels: Add branching logic immediately after Start.
Create an Enterprise outcome that compares the triggering Account's AnnualRevenue with 1,000,000.
Click + after Start > Decision; label it Segment by Revenue; label the outcome Enterprise; set $Record > AnnualRevenue, Greater Than or Equal, 1000000; click Done.

steps.action: Add a Create Records element named Create Enterprise Follow-Up on the Enterprise branch to create one Task assigned to the Account owner.
steps.where: Enterprise connector > Add Element > Data > Create Records.
steps.why: Qualified enterprise Accounts receive a concrete follow-up action.
steps.checkpoint: The Enterprise connector leads to a Create Enterprise Follow-Up card configured for the Task object.
hint_levels: Build the action only on the Enterprise outcome.
Create one Task and populate its owner, related Account, subject, status, and priority.

From Enterprise click + > Create Records; choose One record and Use separate resources and literal values; select Task; set OwnerId to $Record.OwnerId, WhatId to $Record.Id, Subject to Review new enterprise customer, Status to Not Started, and Priority to High; click Done.

steps.action: Connect the Default Outcome directly to the end of the Flow.
steps.where: Default Outcome connector beneath Segment by Revenue on the canvas.
steps.why: Accounts with blank or sub-threshold revenue exit safely without attempting enterprise work.
steps.checkpoint: The Default Outcome path ends without a Create Records element.
hint_levels: The non-enterprise branch needs no action.
Leave the default route as an intentional no-op ending.
Drag the Default Outcome connector to the End node, or leave it unconnected if the canvas uses implicit path endings.

steps.action: Add a Create Records fault handler named Log Task Creation Error from the red fault connector of Create Enterprise Follow-Up.
steps.where: Create Enterprise Follow-Up card > red Fault connector > Add Element > Data > Create Records.
steps.why: A failed Task insertion is captured instead of becoming an unexplained Flow error.
steps.checkpoint: A red connector leads from Create Enterprise Follow-Up to Log Task Creation Error.
hint_levels: Use the error route attached to the Task-creation element.
The red Fault connector should create one Flow_Error__c record.
Select Create Enterprise Follow-Up, drag its red Fault connector, choose Create Records, and label it Log Task Creation Error.

steps.action: Configure Log Task Creation Error to store the fault message and triggering Account ID in a Flow_Error__c record.
steps.where: Log Task Creation Error configuration panel under Set Field Values for the Flow_Error__c Record.
steps.why: The log identifies both the failed operation and the Account that triggered it.
steps.checkpoint: The element shows Flow_Error__c with Message__c mapped to $Flow.FaultMessage and Record_Id__c mapped to $Record.Id.
hint_levels: Capture the system error and the source record.
Map Message__c from the global fault message and Record_Id__c from the triggering Account.
Choose Object Flow_Error__c; set Message__c = $Flow.FaultMessage and Record_Id__c = $Record.Id; click Done.

steps.action: Save the Flow as Qualify Enterprise Accounts and Create Follow-Up.
steps.why: Saving runs validation and creates a version you can test before activation.
steps.checkpoint: The Flow name appears in the header and no validation errors appear.
hint_levels: Name the completed automation from the toolbar.
Use a descriptive label and accept the generated API name.
Click Save, enter Flow Label Qualify Enterprise Accounts and Create Follow-Up, keep the generated Flow API Name, then click Save.

steps.action: Debug the Flow with an Account that meets the entry conditions and has Annual Revenue of at least 1000000.
steps.where: Flow Builder toolbar > Debug > Record-Triggered Flow debug panel.
steps.why: A qualifying test confirms the Enterprise route and Task creation before users rely on it.
steps.checkpoint: Debug Details shows the Enterprise outcome executed and Create Enterprise Follow-Up completed successfully.
hint_levels: Test with a sandbox Account that qualifies for the enterprise branch.
Select an Account with Type Customer - Direct, a Billing Country, and Annual Revenue of at least 1,000,000, then run the debug as an updated record.
Click Debug; choose a qualifying Account; select the updated-record trigger option if shown; enable rollback mode for a non-persistent test; click Run and inspect Debug Details.

steps.why: Activation makes the validated version respond to real Account changes.
steps.checkpoint: The Flow header displays Active and the Flows list shows the version as active.
hint_levels: Use the status control in the Flow Builder toolbar.
Activate only after the qualifying debug follows the expected path.
Close Debug Details if open, click Activate in the upper-right toolbar, and confirm the header status is Active.
